Clear Admit shines a spotlight on LBS MBA students

Six students from LBS’s latest MBA intake reveal what drew them to LBS and their hopes for the future

26 October 2026
Degree EducationDegree programmesFeatured newsSchool communityStudents
Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 2:16
Instaread

London Business School MBA Class of 2028 students Ellen Ehrnrooth, Sofia Castillo Guerrero, Charles Jennison, Nicolas Lozano Landinez, Eva Stewart and Karan Vir Malhotra have been profiled by Clear Admit in its Real Humans: MBA Students series.

Ellen, a dual citizen of Finland and the USA, who was born and raised in London in a Swedish-speaking household, has opted to do an MBA to see what other skills she might have beyond public policy analysis with a view to diversifying her future path.

Sofia from Colombia was motivated to do an MBA as the leaders she admired at work all had one thing in common: an MBA. She’s looking to broaden her perspective and discover possibilities beyond retail. She chose LBS for the diversity of the class.

Charles, from New Zealand, is keen to develop his management and strategy skills for the next stage of his career. He was attracted to LBS by its London location and how highly LBS alumni speak about their experience.

Colombian Nicolas, who was raised in Florida in the USA, spent 8 years in the US army before joining LBS. He’s looking to move into defence technology investing and was also attracted by the London location and international aspect of the LBS MBA.

Eva, from Western Australia, wants to move into an executive leadership role in the mining industry and serve as a role model for people coming up through that industry. She brings unique insight as a young, Indigenous woman in a male-dominated industry.

Kuwaiti Karan sees business school as an opportunity to broaden his perspective and leadership style before returning to the family office to, amongst other things, develop his own investment track record across public and private markets.

Three key pieces of advice for prospective students:

  • Be personal in your essays. Expressing your own story and opinion will make you stand out more

  • Have candid conversations with alumni as their insights into the classroom, careers, clubs, etc. will paint a rich picture of the communities you are hoping to join. Visit campus if you can

  • Start GMAT/GRE prep early.

Privacy Preference Center

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
More information

Manage Consent Preferences

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
